name: Fermentation & Baking Science

objectives.text: Identify common foods made through fermentation, such as bread, yogurt, sauerkraut, and pickles
Identify the basic ingredients of bread and the farm crops they come from
Describe how yeast produces gas that makes bread dough rise
Conduct a simple experiment to observe how sugar and water temperature affect yeast activity
Explain that yeast and bacteria used in fermentation are living microorganisms that feed on sugars
Describe how people in different cultures and times have used fermentation and baking to make and keep food
Explain how yeast and bacteria convert sugars into carbon dioxide, alcohol, or acids during fermentation
Compare yeast fermentation with lactic acid fermentation and name foods produced by each
Explain how chemical leaveners such as baking soda and baking powder produce gas through acid and base reactions
Compare how wheat classes differ in protein content and which baked goods each class best suits
Explain the process of fermentation and its applications in food, feed, and industrial production
Analyze how temperature and time affect the rate of fermentation in a dough or culture sample
Analyze how fermentation changes the flavor, texture, nutritional profile, and shelf life of a food
Analyze how gluten development and leavening agents determine the structure and volume of a baked product
Explain the roles of starch gelatinization, protein coagulation, and Maillard browning during baking
Calculate baker's percentages to scale a bread formula for a production batch
Analyze the ingredient statement on a commercial bread or fermented product label to identify leaveners, cultures, and additives
Monitor pH and acidity during a fermentation to determine when the product is safe and finished
Evaluate the purpose of dough conditioners, enzymes, and other additives used in commercial baking
Compare food fermentation with the fermentation used to produce ethanol from grain and other biomass
Analyze how commercial bakeries and fermentation facilities use biochemistry to develop new food products
Evaluate a baked product using sensory and physical tests such as volume, crumb, and texture and recommend formula changes
Formulate a fermented or baked product and justify the science behind each ingredient and process step
Develop a plan for a value-added fermented or baked product enterprise suitable for a supervised agricultural experience

changes: Kept and reworded all six original objectives. Added competencies on bread ingredients and their crop sources, yeast experiments, microorganisms, history of fermentation, lactic versus yeast fermentation, chemical leaveners, wheat classes, effects of fermentation on food qualities, baking reactions, baker's percentages, label analysis, pH monitoring, commercial additives, ethanol comparison, industry product development, product evaluation, and an SAE value-added enterprise plan. Left general preservation, processing methods, and dairy and meat processing to sibling sub-topics. Assigned AFNR codes only to grade 9 and above objectives where the standard is directly taught.
